title: P1 Hosted API: Progressive Latency Bloom — mitigation notes & runbook draft
content:
Executive summary:

On 2027-11-01 we observed a progressive p95/p99 latency increase ("latency bloom") affecting a subset of hosted-api streaming sessions for ~45 minutes. Impact: customer requests in eu-west and us-central saw median streaming step-up latency go from ~60ms to 320ms and p99 to >2.8s. 5xx rate remained low overall (~0.2%) but user-visible streaming stalls and reconnections rose. Trigger: a KV cache eviction cascade combined with an autoscaler drain interaction (nodes being cordoned for patching in two clusters), amplifying tail latencies under normal bursty traffic.

Why this doc exists (scope):
- Capture rapid triage, temporary mitigations, and an initial runbook template for "latency bloom" pattern (distinct from sudden 5xx waves).
- Provide reproducible telemetry queries and playbook steps for oncall and SRE responders.
- Track follow-ups and owners for permanent fixes.

Incident timeline (high-level):
- 08:03 UTC: Alert fired — streaming p95 > 500ms on edge-pop eu-west.
- 08:06 UTC: SRE oncall (Tomás) acknowledges; begins correlation with autoscaler events and K/V cache metrics.
- 08:08 UTC: Observed increase in KV cache eviction rates and a sharp rise in shard miss latencies.
- 08:10 UTC: Canary routing shows a subset of nodes with high KV lease renew attempt rates and increased queue depth.
- 08:15 UTC: Engineering confirms scheduled drain operations in us-central and eu-west due to rolling patch window (ops-run RINF-4518).
- 08:20 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied — route new streaming sessions away from affected nodes to warm pools; reduce allowed batch window from 35ms -> 15ms for streaming router.
- 08:35 UTC: p95 back to ~140ms; p99 trending down but intermittent spikes persist during concurrent drains.
- 08:45 UTC: Deployed emergency backoff/repair for KV prefetcher to reduce evictions (feature-flag); p99 stabilizes under 600ms.
- 08:48 UTC: Incident downgraded to P1 impact and moved to monitoring.

Root cause hypothesis (initial):
- Primary factors: concurrent node drains (autoscaler patch job) + uneven traffic redistribution -> KV cache working set rebalancing and eviction cascade.
- Secondary: streaming router's batching mechanics caused brief head-of-line amplification on nodes that lost large KV prefixes; combined with small-number hot prefixes (prefix skew) this intensified tail latency.
- Not root: no single software bug was found in serving runtime; no hardware/network partition detected.

Key signals used for triage (queries and dashboards):
- PromQL for p95 streaming: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(streaming_step_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])))
- KV eviction rate: rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[30s]) by (shard)
- KV miss latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(kv_lookup_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])))
- Node drain events: increase(kube_node_drain_total[5m]) and kube_pod_eviction{reason=\"drain\"}
- Router batch/window size traces: tracing tag router.batch_window_ms (edge-span)
- Customer-visible errors: sum(rate(hosted_api_stream_reconnect_total[1m])) by (region)

Immediate mitigations (what we did):
- Short-term routing: route new sessions to warm pools with >30m uptime to preserve large KV caches (applied via router policy /routes/streaming-v2 fallback).
- Reduced batch window for streaming router to lower head-of-line delays (from 35ms to 15ms).
- Throttled concurrent prefetches per-shard (FF) to reduce eviction pressure.
- Halted non-critical autoscaler drain jobs in eu-west/us-central until warm pools scaled up (coord with platform ops).
- Customer communication: incident page updated with ETA: \"partial impact, mitigation in progress\".

Runbook draft (for future oncalls) — progressive latency bloom pattern:
Trigger conditions (alert thresholds):
- p95_streaming_duration > 300ms for >= 3m in two adjacent regions OR
- sustained increase in kv_cache_evictions_total > 5x normal baseline in any shard for 2m

Immediate triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Acknowledge and set channel (#sre-incident-<id>).
2) Collect region-level p95/p99, KV eviction and miss metrics, and node drain events.
3) Query which nodes are being cordoned/drained and their last restart times.
4) If drains present -> route new sessions away from draining nodes.
5) Temporarily reduce router batch window to 15ms (per-region) via router config.
6) Toggle KV prefetch throttle FF if eviction surge observed.
7) Escalate to platform ops if concurrent automated drains are active.

Containment playbook (during incident):
- If p99 > 2s or reconnects > baseline*3: enable emergency routing to warm pools + autoscale warm pool (scale up by 30%).
- If eviction cascade persists after routing change: apply per-shard prefetch backoff and set kv_cache_max_evict_rate soft-limit.
- If customer errors increase AND 5xx>1%: consider temporary selective degrading: turn off large-prefix prefetch for low-tier traffic.

Recovery validation steps:
- p95 and p99 must be trending down for >10m and KV eviction rate at baseline for >5m.
- No new reconnect bursts.
- Confirm drains completed and nodes fully rejoined with warm caches.

Post-incident follow-ups (owners and tickets):
- RINF-4521 (Tomás) — investigate autoscaler scheduling overlap with warm-pool maintenance windows; propose safety gate.
- RINF-4522 (Maya) — add adaptive prefetcher backoff that reacts to global eviction signals.
- RINF-4523 (Ethan) — router change: expose regional batch_window_ms as per-route runtime flag and add auto-lower on detected tail amplification.
- RINF-4524 (Riley) — improve telemetry: add per-prefix heatmap for KV misses to identify hot-prefix skew earlier.

Notes / open questions (brainstorm, not finalized):
- Why did warm-pool routing not automatically protect sessions? existing routing logic prefers local-pop affinity and may have insufficient cost for warm-vs-cold preference. Could adopt weight bias to prefer warm node uptime above affinity during drains.
- Can we better coordinate patch windows to avoid multiple clusters draining concurrently in the same customer-facing regions? (ops policy item).
- Is there a cost-effective TTL or shadow-warming strategy for prefix-heavy workloads to avoid mass eviction on rebalancing?

Proposed medium-term mitigations (2–8 weeks):
- Adaptive prefetch backoff (RINF-4522).
- Router auto-thin: dynamic batch-window tuner that reduces window when tail latency rises (RINF-4523).
- Warm-pool scheduling safety gate in autoscaler to avoid overlapping drains across region rings (RINF-4521).
- Add a streaming SLO playbook page with explicit guidance for differentiating latency bloom vs head-on-load spikes.

Long-term engineering projects (quarter-plus):
- Replace global eviction counters with a coherent lease-based prefetch placement to limit cascade effects.
- Investigate cross-region KV prefix replication for ultra-hot prefixes to reduce cross-node miss amplification.

Communications and customer impact notes:
- Affected customers: subset of streaming customers in eu-west & us-central heavy with prefix-skew workloads. No broad data loss; user-visible reconnects and step-up latency caused degraded UX.
- Post-incident customer comms: targeted outreach recommended for customers with > 5 reconnects during window (owned by CS lead).

Appendix — quick ops commands and queries:
- Get list of draining nodes: kubectl get nodes -l drain=true -o wide
- PromQL: sum by (region) (rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[1m]))
- Trace example: search for spans with tag router.batch_window_ms>25 and duration>1s
- Router toggle: curl -XPOST $ROUTER_ADMIN/flags -d '{\"streaming.batch_window_ms\":15}' (authorized)

Draft status and next steps:
- This is a working draft (SRE runbook seed). Needs: playbook validation in game day, automated runbook steps in PagerDuty actions, and doc->confluence migration for the finalized runbook.
- Owner for runbook publication: Tomás Ortega (target: after RINF-4522 & RINF-4523 merged).

Raw notes captured from channel (#sre-incident-4521):
- \"noticed eviction curve at 08:07; drains scheduled at 08:05 by ops pipeline\" — Maya
- \"reduced batch window -> immediate p95 improvement but p99 still twitchy\" — Tomás
- \"we should flag warm-pool affinity in routing, seems like the missing piece\" — Riley
